newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bids at about $4.50 premium for A-180 - trader.
newsitem.headline: Japan bids at about $4.50 premium for A-180 - trader.

text.p: Japanese firms bid at about $4.50 over the Aramco formula for Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura A-180 term naphtha cargoes for 1997, while South Korean firms bid at a premium of $3.40, traders said on Monday.

In the term naphtha tender that closed last Friday, Japanese trading houses were likely to have bid at around $4.50 above the formula for the A-180, paraffinic naphtha favoured among petrochemical end-users, traders said.
They also said three South Korean firms all placed bids with a $3.40 premium.
The premium for A-180 cargoes was set at $3.40 above the Aramco formula for the second half of 1996, and at $4.00 for the August 1996-July 1997 period.
The new premium for 1997 is expected to be set by the end of October, traders said.
